identity.name: Švitrigaila's Grand Duchy
native_names: Švitrigailos Rusios Didžioji Kunigaikštystė (Švitrigaila's Ruthenian grand duchy)

land.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

predecessors.note: Švitrigaila had been elected grand duke in October 1430 and was overthrown on the night of 31 August 1432 (Švitrigaila page); his supporters then held the east.

land.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

successors.note: Sigismund Kęstutaitis's side won at Wiłkomierz in 1435; Švitrigaila withdrew to Moldavia in 1438 and the lands returned to the Grand Duchy (Casimir IV was approved as grand duke in 1440).

capitals.name: Polotsk
capitals.note: The Švitrigaila page gives no seat for his rule; he escaped to Polotsk after the coup of 1432 and fled there again after 1435. The coordinates are the town's, not from the page.

rulers.name: Švitrigaila
rulers.title: Grand Duke of Ruthenia
rulers.note: The infobox lists him as 'Grand Duke of Ruthenia' for 1432-1440 and as grand duke of Lithuania from October 1430 to 31 August 1432.

correction.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the coup of 31 August 1432 the Civil War page puts 'Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev, and Volhynia' with Švitrigaila's supporters and 'the Lithuanian lands, Samogitia, Trakai Voivodeship, and Minsk' with Sigismund Kęstutaitis; the Švitrigaila page repeats the east for Švitrigaila. No page gives borders or when each town changed sides (Švitrigaila's army was beaten at Wiłkomierz in September 1435 and 'losing influence, he fled to Polotsk'); Cliopatria draws one undivided Lithuania for 1431-1449.

region.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

ledger.note: 31 August 1432: Švitrigaila is overthrown in Lithuania and keeps the east. 'Conspirators, led by Sigismund Kęstutaitis, attacked Švitrigaila and his escort, who were staying in Ashmyany'; he escaped to Polotsk, and the Lithuanian nobles split into two camps, Švitrigaila's in 'Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev, and Volhynia'. The infobox calls him 'Grand Duke of Ruthenia' for 1432-1440.

region.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

ledger.note: 1432: the east passes to Švitrigaila's side. The Civil War page: 'Švitrigaila's supporters held Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev, and Volhynia'; it dates the coup to 31 August 1432 and gives no dates for the other lands.

region.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

ledger.note: 1438: Švitrigaila withdraws to Moldavia and the east returns to the Grand Duchy. 'Švitrigaila withdraws to Moldavia' in 1438; in September 1437 he had proposed to rule the lands that still backed him, 'chiefly Kiev and Volhynia', which the Polish Senate did not ratify (Švitrigaila page).

region.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

ledger.note: 1438: the rival grand duchy ends. The lead of the Civil War page says Švitrigaila surrendered in 1437 and the war ended in 'decisive defeat for Švitrigaila'; he returned in 1440 'to rule Podolia and Volhynia' (Švitrigaila page) and died in Lutsk on 10 February 1452.

wars.name: Lithuanian Civil War (1432-1438)

zones.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, the lands of Švitrigaila's supporters

wars.outcome: Sigismund Kęstutaitis, backed by Poland, defeated Švitrigaila, backed by the Teutonic Knights, at Wiłkomierz in September 1435; Švitrigaila withdrew to Moldavia in 1438; Sigismund was assassinated in 1440 and Casimir IV approved as grand duke.
wars.note: Truce of Jasiniec 13 September 1433; Peace of Brześć Kujawski 31 December 1435, after which the Knights stopped backing Švitrigaila.

certainty.note: The pages name the lands of the two sides by town and region only; no frontier between them is given.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks: Cliopatria draws one undivided Grand Duchy of Lithuania for 1431-1449. The extent is the Civil War page's list of Švitrigaila's supporters' lands (Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev, Volhynia); the pages do not date when each came or went, so the span 1432-1438 is the page's outer span and the loss and gain are confidence 2 on the year only. The dossier is written by batch eu-15-h from the two pages above. Podolia (which Švitrigaila ruled after 1440, with Volhynia) is outside the span. Gazetteer: no new names.
